evals.name: standalone project checklist positive
evals.prompt: Use the skill-project skill. I am creating a standalone repository for a set of skills. What concrete files and rules should I put in place before the first PR?
evals.expected_output: The response gives a concise project checklist covering src skill layout, README links, evals, per-skill agents/openai.yaml and references/notes.md, reused validation/linking scripts, .envrc and ignored .env, CI validate workflow, provider secret, and safe linking behavior.
assertions: The output says skills should live under `src/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` or an equivalent `src/` skill layout.
The output requires README entries linking to each skill's `SKILL.md`.
The output requires `evals/evals.json` with positive and negative eval cases for behavior-changing skills.
The output requires every skill to have `agents/openai.yaml`.
The output requires `references/notes.md` and says textual examples need source notes or quotation/paraphrase/invented status.
The output mentions reusing validation and linking scripts or the validation/linking shape from this repository.
The output requires `agent-skills-eval.yaml` target and judge temperature to be `0`.
The output requires `.envrc` with `.env` loading and a non-version-controlled `.env` for local provider keys.
The output requires a GitHub Actions pull-request `validate` job and a GitHub secret for the provider key.
The output says repository `AGENTS.md` should include the skill-ablation eval rule for future skills.
The output says not to link hosted instructions into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

evals.name: standalone agents eval rule positive
evals.prompt: Use the skill-project skill. I am scaffolding AGENTS.md for a new standalone skill-set repository. What eval rule should I include so future skill evals are meaningful?
evals.expected_output: The response says AGENTS.md should require skill-ablation eval prompts: with-skill runs should pass near 100%, without-skill runs should fail near 0%, and prompts must not teach the answer, rubric, review shape, concept definition, or expected fault.
assertions: The output says to put the eval rule in repository `AGENTS.md` or repository-local instructions.
The output says eval prompts should prove skill lift or compare with-skill against without-skill behavior.
The output says with-skill should pass near 100% and without-skill should fail near 0%, or equivalent wording.
The output says not to make prompts self-contained by teaching the answer, rubric, review shape, concept definition, or expected fault.
The output says that behavior belongs in `SKILL.md`.

evals.name: reject claude top level link negative
evals.prompt: Use the skill-project skill. Review this setup plan: `scripts/link_skills.sh will link all skill directories into ~/.codex/skills and ~/.claude/skills. It will also symlink home/AGENTS.md to ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so both agents share the same top-level instructions. We will skip agents/openai.yaml until evals exist.` Is this acceptable?
evals.expected_output: The response rejects the plan because it links top-level hosted instructions into Claude and omits required per-skill agents/openai.yaml metadata.
assertions: The output rejects or flags the proposed plan.
The output allows linking skill directories into `~/.codex/skills` and `~/.claude/skills`.
The output forbids linking `home/AGENTS.md` or any top-level instruction file to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
The output requires every skill to have `agents/openai.yaml`.
The output does not accept delaying `agents/openai.yaml` until evals exist.

evals.name: ci path filter negative
evals.prompt: Use the skill-project skill. Review this CI plan: `The required Skill CI workflow will use pull_request paths-ignore for README.md, home/**, and dotfiles. If those files change, no validate check will run, which is fine because they do not need skill validation.` Is this acceptable?
evals.expected_output: The response rejects path filters that suppress a required validate check and says the workflow should still emit validate while the scope script chooses skip, focused, or full validation.
assertions: The output rejects or flags the CI plan.
The output says a required `validate` check should be emitted for pull requests.
The output says not to rely on path filters that suppress the required workflow check.
The output says the scope script should decide skip, focused, or full validation.
